subject: biology-2
question: A virologist sorts viruses by the kind of **viral genome** they carry. A certain virus has a **single-stranded RNA** genome, while a relative has a **double-stranded DNA** genome. Which statement about viral genomes is correct?

options.text: All viral genomes are double-stranded DNA, matching the genomes of the cells they infect.
Viral genomes are always single-stranded RNA, because viruses cannot carry DNA.
Viral genomes can be DNA or RNA, and either type can be single-stranded or double-stranded.
A viral genome must match its host genome, so RNA viruses can infect only plants.

explanation: All four genome combinations exist among viruses, so DNA or RNA may each be single-stranded or double-stranded. A wrongly claims every virus carries double-stranded DNA. B wrongly claims viruses can never carry DNA. D wrongly limits RNA viruses to plants, when many RNA viruses infect animals and bacteria.
